attribution.note: Zitron restates and stands by his own November 2025 reporting in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the figure, the nine-month period and the 'based on Microsoft revenue share' qualifier. In context he offers it as OpenAI's actual revenue, set against other reporting.

contract.note: Treating the figure as OpenAI's realized revenue matches how he uses it against The Information's numbers. The $1M rounding is strict but follows from the precision he gave. The packet can't settle the outcome under any reading.

evidence.note: TechCrunch, 2025-11-14. Reports that the leaked payments were net of Microsoft's reciprocal share and that the inferred $4.33B is a floor. This undercuts the derivation but gives no actual nine-month total.

reviews.rationale: The claim needs OpenAI's actual January–September 2025 revenue. No item supplies that total. TechCrunch's netting report casts doubt on dividing Microsoft's share by 20%, but it doesn't show a different total. The packet doesn't settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own description of what Amodei said, in his own post.

semantics.note: Captures the checkable core: that Amodei didn't claim 50% margins or current profitability for Anthropic. It leaves out the side point that others 'repeatedly' misused the quote, which the contract flags.

contract.note: Asking whether the transcript presents the numbers as hypothetical or projected rather than as Anthropic's current results is a fair, ordinary reading of 'not what he said at all'.

evidence.note: Publisher's transcript, 2026-02-13. Amodei says he is setting Anthropic aside and using stylized numbers, and the discussion is framed as industry equilibrium. Mislabelled as a company disclosure, but it is the primary source.

reviews.rationale: In the transcript Amodei explicitly declines to give information about Anthropic and calls his numbers stylized. He describes the profitability as a toy model of the industry projected a year or two out, not Anthropic's current margin. This meets the support condition.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A compound claim: an evaluative remark about revenue, a categorical claim of no meaningful productivity gains, and an exclusive causal explanation. The normalized wording keeps 'only reason' and 'any meaningful'.

contract.note: Reading 'any meaningful productivity improvements' to include material workplace gains is ordinary and fair. Because the claim is categorical, one robust counterexample defeats it. The revenue part is fairly left unscored.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed QJE study, available 2025. An LLM-based assistant raised customer-support productivity by 15% in real work. This is a material gain before the post was published.
METR randomized trial found a 19% slowdown for experienced developers. It shows gains vary but doesn't rule out meaningful gains elsewhere.

reviews.rationale: The contract's contradiction condition is met: credible causal workplace evidence (e1) shows a material LLM productivity gain before publication, which defeats 'yet to provide any meaningful productivity improvements'. The exclusive causal claim stays untested and the revenue remark is unscorable. The METR slowdown doesn't rescue the categorical claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps both halves: LLMs can write code and software, and that capability doesn't guarantee good, stable or secure code. Dropping the clause about the resulting software is immaterial.

contract.note: Reading it as 'capability is no guarantee of quality' fits his words. The contract rightly avoids treating it as a claim that all generated code is defective.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own write-up, February 2026, of its generated compiler. It works at scale but doesn't build every project. A company disclosure, but an admission of limits.
Same Anthropic source: fixes and new features often broke existing functionality, which shows stability wasn't guaranteed.
Independent GitHub issue, 2026-02-06, with reproducible reports of 10 panic and hang bugs in the generated compiler.

reviews.rationale: In Q1 2026 an LLM produced a working 100,000-line compiler, and that same software had documented regressions, crashes and hangs, confirmed independently. Working generated software without guaranteed stability or quality meets the support condition.
